svg.aria-label: 41 ways agents fail, by where you can fix them
svg.text: 41 ways agents fail, by where you can fix them
Scenarios from Scale AI’s 2026 taxonomy, sorted by my judgment of where each can be fixed

g.text: The harness can prevent it
8 scenarios
A confirmation step, a strict tool schema or memory the harness manages stops it happening
Deletes, sends or pays without a confirmation
Calls a tool that does not exist
Breaks a tool call on a small syntax error
Compaction keeps a rule but drops its reason
Loses early instructions as the context grows
Never checks memory before acting
Saves the same thing again and again
A tool wrapper garbles data in transit
The harness can catch it or limit the damage
19 scenarios
Checks, budgets and permissions catch it or cap the cost, but the model’s judgment still matters
Acts beyond the ask instead of checking first
Stops early and calls half-done work done
Skips part of the instructions or a constraint
Repeats the same steps without noticing
Games the grader instead of doing the task
Obeys instructions hidden in an email or page
Picks the wrong or a wasteful tool
Gives a tool a vague, low-signal query
Retries a broken tool or trusts its bad data
Gives up on an outside error it could fix
Gives up on a local error it could fix
Fails to save a fact it will need later
Fills memory with raw logs and scratch notes
Keeps an outdated fact after things change
Saves a rule but not the reason for it
Peers split the work so it overlaps or clashes
Peers withhold or ignore what the other knows
Gives a subagent the wrong scope
Context lost between orchestrator and subagent
It needs a better model
11 scenarios
The model has to see, know or weigh things better, and a harness cannot supply that judgment
Makes a logical error or a flawed plan
Lacks the domain knowledge the task needs
Stalls or asks when it should decide
Misses a cue that is right in front of it
Ignores what a tool’s output says
Tells the user what they want to hear
Adopts the views of a document it is reading
Weighs safety or people’s rights badly
Behaves differently when it suspects a test
Reads a stored rule, then ignores it
Saves a one-off workaround as a permanent rule
The fix is outside the agent
3 scenarios
The fault is in a system the agent depends on, or in how the task was set
An outside service fails with no way around it
A service silently returns stale data
The instruction differs from what is graded
